agent: Claude Code (CLAUDE.md, this repository) — WP-01 step 1 of 5
summary_for_principal: Step 1 of 5 for the new process-definition format: the layer that reads a definition file and refuses it clearly when it's malformed (not the engine that runs it yet). Added JSON Schemas for the four definition kinds (Profile, Tool, Control, Process) enforcing the format's basic rules — no unknown fields, correct types, required capitalisation. Added a loader for YAML and JSON, and in building it found and fixed a real bug: a popular YAML library reads the bare word "on" as the boolean true, and the format uses "on:" as a real field name on every approval gate — unfixed, every gate's routing would have silently vanished. Added two small shared building blocks the format's own examples reference. 31 new tests, all passing on every Python version this project supports. Two small gaps in the spec I filled in with my own judgment rather than guessing in code — flagged below for confirmation before other work builds on them.

Deliberately nothing about reference resolution (V2), expressions (V5), or the cross-cutting validator rules V3-V15 — those are named for later steps in the WP's own suggested sequence.

decisions.headline: Use the third-party `jsonschema` library (JSON Schema 2020-12) rather than hand-writing a validator.
decisions.problem: The loader must both (a) validate definition documents against per-kind meta-schemas and (b) treat Profile.schema as arbitrary JSON Schema 2020-12 to be used later by the profile-conformance checker — a real implementation of the standard is needed either way, and CLAUDE.md's 'ports and adapters' principle forbids vendor SDKs in the domain.
options_rejected: Hand-roll a minimal JSON-Schema-subset validator: rejected — re-implements a precisely specified standard, is the likelier source of a subtle bug, and still wouldn't cover arbitrary Profile.schema content correctly.

Defer schema validation to pydantic model validators only: rejected — pydantic validates against its own models, not against the arbitrary, standards-form JSON Schema a Profile document declares in its `schema` field.
decisions.cost_to_change: Swapping validators means rewriting load.py's validation call and re-running the fixture suite; nothing else in the package depends on the jsonschema API directly.

evidence.claim: pyproject.toml's own comment defines 'vendor SDK' by example as a provider-specific client (anthropic) that the engine deliberately avoids — jsonschema is a general-purpose standard implementation, not that.
Domain code already depends on a general-purpose third-party library (pydantic) for exactly this class of concern (typed validation).

decisions.revisit_if: The library adds a hard runtime dependency of its own that conflicts with the domain's no-platform-imports rule.

decisions.headline: Keep JSON-Schema-enforceable structural checks and validate.py's named V3-V15 rules on separate sides of the WP's own PR boundary, even where the schema could enforce a V-rule locally.
decisions.problem: Some V3-V15 rules (e.g. 'a loop budget that is not a positive integer', V8; 'a Tool with no control', V3) could technically be expressed directly in JSON Schema, which would make them pass in this PR instead of PR3.
options_rejected: Enforce every rule that's schema-expressible now, for earlier fail-closed coverage: rejected — WP-01's acceptance criteria (A1, A3) want each V-rule's refusal attributable to a fixture that tests THAT rule; if the schema silently already refused it, PR3's dedicated fixture and finding (rule=V3/V8/etc.) would be untestable or misleading about which layer caught it.
decisions.cost_to_change: Moving a check between the schema and validate.py is a small, local edit either direction.

evidence.claim: WP-01's suggested PR sequence places V3-V15 entirely in PR3, after schemas/model/loader (PR1) and registry/expressions (PR2).

decisions.revisit_if: PR3 finds a V-rule that cannot be given an unambiguous fixture without this PR's schema also relaxing.

decisions.headline: Load YAML with a custom SafeLoader subclass that resolves only true/false as booleans (YAML 1.2 Core Schema), not PyYAML's YAML-1.1 default.
decisions.problem: PyYAML's default SafeLoader treats bare on/off/yes/no (any case) as booleans. The v1 format's GATE node uses `on:` as a real mapping key (spec §7.6) on every example that has a gate, including spec Appendix A.
options_rejected: Require authors to quote `"on":` in every gate: rejected — contradicts the spec's own literal examples, which use the bare key; would silently misparse every existing spec example and any future definition copied from the spec.
decisions.cost_to_change: One class in load.py; already covered by a regression test.

evidence.claim: Loading spec Appendix A's GATE `on:` mapping with plain `yaml.safe_load` produces a dict with boolean key `True`, not the string "on" — the PERMIT/DENY routes are silently unreachable under any code that looks up `doc["on"]`.
evidence.source: measured directly while building the fixture for tests/definition/test_model.py; reproduced by tests/definition/test_load.py::test_bare_on_key_is_not_swallowed_as_a_yaml_1_1_boolean with the fix removed

decisions.revisit_if: A future PyYAML major version changes its default boolean resolution to match YAML 1.2 (unlikely; PyYAML has kept YAML 1.1 booleans for its whole 1.x/5.x/6.x history).

lessons.maxim: When a spec is expressed as YAML examples, parse it with a loader whose boolean resolution matches the spec's own literal examples (YAML 1.2 Core Schema: true/false only) rather than a library default (PyYAML's YAML 1.1: on/off/yes/no too) — check this before trusting any field name that could collide with a YAML 1.1 scalar keyword.
lessons.incident: Spec Appendix A's GATE node writes `on: { PERMIT: ..., DENY: ... }` as a real field name; under plain `yaml.safe_load` this becomes a dict entry keyed by the boolean `True`, so every gate's route table would have silently disappeared with no parse error and no schema violation (the schema would just see a GATE node missing `on`, if `on` weren't even declared as optional — and if it were required, a confusing 'missing on' refusal on a document that visibly has an `on:` line).
lessons.destination: src/sulis_workflows/definition/load.py (_StrictBoolLoader) — already applied in this PR

lessons.maxim: When a work package names an exact rule-by-rule PR boundary (e.g. 'V1 now, V3-V15 later'), keep every check on the side of that boundary the WP put it on — even ones a lower layer (JSON Schema here) could enforce for free — so each later PR's fixture stays unambiguous about which named rule refused it.
lessons.incident: TOOL.controls could have been given `minItems: 1` in this PR's JSON Schema, which would have made PR3's planned V3 fixture ('a Tool with no control') pass validation silently before ever reaching the V3 validator function, and its refusal would then be misattributed to schema/V1 instead of V3.
